paragraphs.text: Children’s Discovery Museum
General Information about Group Play
Pricing
Group Play        7/person
Scholarships
We offer scholarships to low-income schools and youth organizations, subject to availability. Participation in a post-visit survey is required.
Scholarships are for Group Play admission fees and/or transportation. Transportation invoices (发票) must be received within 60 days of your visit to guarantee the scholarship.
Group Size
We require one chaperone (监护人) per ten children. Failure to provide enough chaperones will result in an extra charge of 50 per absent adult.
Group Play is for groups of 10 or more with a limit of 35 people. For groups of 35 or more, please call to discuss options.
Hours
The Museum is open daily from 9:30 am to 4:30 pm.
Group Play may be scheduled during any day or time the Museum is open.
Registration Policy
Registration must be made at least two weeks in advance.
Register online or fill out a Group Play Registration Form with multiple date and start time options.
Once the registration form is received and processed, we will send a confirmation email within two business days.
Guidelines
● Teachers and chaperones should model good behavior for the group and remain with students at all times.
● Children are not allowed unaccompanied in all areas of the Museum.
● Children should play nicely with each other and exhibits.
● Use your indoor voice when at the Museum.
We journalists live in a new age of storytelling, with many new multimedia tools. Many young people don’t even realize it’s new. For them, it’s just normal.

This hit home for me as I was sitting with my 2-year-old grandson on a sofa over the Spring Festival holiday. I had brought a children’s book to read. It had simple words and colorful pictures – a perfect match for his age.
Picture this: my grandson sitting on my lap as I hold the book in front so he can see the pictures. As I read, he reaches out and pokes (戳) the page with his finger.

What’s up with that? He just likes the pictures, I thought. Then I turned the page and continued. He poked the page even harder. I nearly dropped the book. I was confused: Is there something wrong with this kid?

Then I realized what was happening. He was actually a stranger to books. His father frequently amused the boy with a tablet computer which was loaded with colorful pictures that come alive when you poke them. He thought my storybook was like that.

Sorry, kid. This book is not part of your high-tech world. It’s an outdated, lifeless thing. An antique, like your grandfather. Well, I may be old, but I’m not hopelessly challenged, digitally speaking. I edit video and produce audio. I use mobile payment. I’ve even built websites.

There’s one notable gap in my new-media experience, however. I’ve spent little time in front of a camera, since I have a face made for radio. But that didn’t stop China Daily from asking me last week to share a personal story for a video project about the integration of Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei province.
Anyway, grandpa is now an Internet star – two minutes of fame! I promise not to let it go to my head. But I will make sure my 2-year-old grandson sees it on his tablet.

Over the last seven years, most states have banned texting by drivers, and public service campaigns have tried a wide range of methods to persuade people to put down their phones when they are behind the wheel.

Yet the problem, by just about any measure, appears to be getting worse. Americans are still texting while driving, as well as using social networks and taking photos. Road accidents, which had fallen for years, are now rising sharply.
That is partly because people are driving more, but Mark Rosekind, the chief of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, said distracted (分心) driving was “only increasing, unfortunately”.

“Big change requires big ideas,” he said in a speech last month, referring broadly to the need to improve road safety. So to try to change a distinctly modern behavior, lawmakers and public health experts are reaching back to an old approach: They want to treat distracted driving like drunk driving.

An idea from lawmakers in New York is to give police officers a new device called the Textalyzer. It would work like this: An officer arriving at the scene of a crash could ask for the phones of the drivers and use the Textalyzer to check in the operating system for recent activity. The technology could determine whether a driver had just texted, emailed or done anything else that is not allowed under New York’s hands-free driving laws.

“We need something on the books that can change people’s behavior,” said Félix W. Ortiz, who pushed for the state’s 2001 ban on hand-held devices by drivers. If the Textalyzer bill becomes law, he said, “people are going to be more afraid to put their hands on the cell phone.”

As we age, even if we’re healthy, the heart just isn’t as efficient in processing oxygen as it used to be. In most people the first signs show up in their 50s or early 60s. And among people who don’t exercise, the changes can start even sooner.

“Think of a rubber band. In the beginning, it is flexible, but put it in a drawer for 20 years and it will become dry and easily broken,” says Dr. Ben Levine, a heart specialist at the University of Texas. That’s what happens to the heart. Fortunately for those in midlife, Levine is finding that even if you haven’t been an enthusiastic exerciser, getting in shape now may help improve your aging heart.

Levine and his research team selected volunteers aged between 45 and 64 who did not exercise much but were otherwise healthy. Participants were randomly divided into two groups. The first group participated in a program of nonaerobic (无氧) exercise – balance training and weight training – three times a week. The second group did high-intensity aerobic exercise under the guidance of a trainer for four or more days a week. After two years, the second group saw remarkable improvements in heart health.

“We took these 50-year-old hearts and turned the clock back to 30- or 35-year-old hearts,” says Levine. “And the reason they got so much stronger and fitter was that their hearts could now fill a lot better and pump (泵送) a lot more blood during exercise.” But the hearts of those who participated in less intense exercise didn’t change, he says.

“The sweet spot in life to start exercising, if you haven’t already, is in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility,” Levine says. “We put healthy 70-year-olds through a yearlong exercise training program, and nothing happened to them at all.”

Dr. Nieca Goldberg, a spokeswoman for the American Heart Association, says Levine’s findings are a great start. But the study was small and needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people to determine exactly which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference.

paragraphs.text: Writing an essay is a difficult process for most people. However, the process can be made easier if you learn to practice three simple techniques.

__36__ 1   When you are first trying to think of ideas for an essay, put your pen to your paper and write nonstop for ten or fifteen minutes without letting your pen leave the paper. Stay loose and free. __37__ 2   Don’t worry about grammar or spelling. Even though this technique won’t work for everyone, it helps many people get a good store of ideas to draw on.

The next technique is to write your draft rapidly without worrying about being perfect. __38__ 3   Yet, by learning to live with imperfection, you will save yourself headaches and a wastepaper basket full of crumpled (弄皱的) paper. Think of your first draft as a path cut out of the jungle – as part of an exploration, not as a complete highway.

The third technique is to try printing out a triple-spaced (三倍行距) copy to allow space for revision. __39__ 4   As a result, these writers never get in the habit of crossing out chunks (大块) of their draft and writing revisions in the blank space. After you have revised your draft until it is too messy to work from anymore, you can enter your changes into your word processor. __40__ 5   The resulting blank space invites you to revise.

Like many young people, Jessica wants to travel the globe. Unlike most of them, this 25-year-old is doing it __41__ . She and her husband have spent the last two years traveling the world, stopping everywhere from Paris to Singapore. It might sound like one long, expensive __42__ , but the couple has an unusual way to make their travel __43__ .
They’re part of a new form of the __44__ economy: an online group of house sitters. Throughout their no-cost stays in __45__ homes, they feed pets and water plants in the homeowner’s __46__ .

It’s not all sightseeing. The two travelers carefully __47__ their trips, scheduling their days around the pets that are sometimes difficult to __48__ . But house sitting also offers a level of __49__ they can’t find in a hotel. “It’s like __50__ at a friend’s house,” Jessica says.

The couple has a high __51__ rate in getting accepted as house sitters and they always go beyond the homeowner’s __52__ . For Jessica, that means __53__ plenty of pictures of happy pets, keeping the house __54__ and leaving a nice small gift before heading to the next house. “You want to make the homeowner feel that they made the right __55__ ,” she says.

Henry Tyler made the catch of the year on the weekend. When he saw a young child hanging from a sixth-floor apartment balcony (阳台) , Henry ran one hundred metres, jumped over a 1.2-metre fence, and held out his arms to catch the __56__ (fall) child.
Eric Brown, only three years old, knocked Henry down when he fell. The boy is in the hospital and doctors say he’ll be OK.

__57__Brown family live in an apartment building outside Toronto. On the day of the accident, Mrs. Brown was at work and Eric was at home with his father. They both fell __58__ (sleep) while watching TV.

Eric woke up a little later when he heard children playing outside. He pushed a chair onto the balcony, and climbed up __59__ (see) them. When he looked down, he __60__ (accidental) slipped and fell over the edge. He hung on for a few minutes __61__screamed for his father, but his father didn’t hear him.
Henry __62__ (fix) his car when he heard the screams. He looked up and saw Eric hanging from the balcony. He quickly __63__ (throw) his tools aside, and started running, arms out.
“He saved my __64__ (son) life,” said Mrs. Brown. “I don’t know __65__to thank him.”
“I just didn’t want the boy to be hurt,” said Henry.
假定你是校广播站英语节目“Talk and Talk”的负责人李华，请给外教Caroline写邮件邀请她做一次访谈。内容包括：
（1）节目介绍；
（2）访谈的时间和话题。注意：
（1）写作词数应为80左右；
（2）可适当增加细节，以使行文连贯。Dear Caroline,
Yours sincerely, Li Hua
It was the day of the big cross-country run. Students from seven different primary schools in and around the small town were warming up and walking the route (路线) through thick evergreen forest.

I looked around and finally spotted David, who was standing by himself off to the side by a fence. He was small for ten years old. His usual big toothy smile was absent today. I walked over and asked him why he wasn’t with the other children. He hesitated and then said he had decided not to run.
What was wrong? He had worked so hard for this event!

I quickly searched the crowd for the school’s coach and asked him what had happened. “I was afraid that kids from other schools would laugh at him,” he explained uncomfortably. “I gave him the choice to run or not, and let him decide.”

I bit back my frustration (懊恼) . I knew the coach meant well – he thought he was doing the right thing. After making sure that David could run if he wanted, I turned to find him coming towards me, his small body rocking from side to side as he swung his feet forward.

David had a brain disease which prevented him from walking or running like other children, but at school his classmates thought of him as a regular kid. He always participated to the best of his ability in whatever they were doing. That was why none of the children thought it unusual that David had decided to join the cross-country team. It just took him longer – that’s all. David had not missed a single practice, and although he always finished his run long after the other children, he did always finish. As a special education teacher at the school, I was familiar with the challenges David faced and was proud of his strong determination.

group-2022-ii-reading-b.overview: 一位资深记者以第一人称记叙散文的方式，借给两岁孙子读纸质绘本时孙子反复戳书页的小事，引出「我们正处在多媒体讲故事的新时代」这一主题，并自嘲式地反思自己作为「老一辈」在数字时代的位置。

discourseStructure.summary: 文章先抛出「新媒体时代」的总论点，再用孙子戳书的具体故事层层设置悬念并揭示原因，随后转入作者对自身数字能力的自我评价，最后以登上视频项目、成为「网络明星」收尾，首尾呼应。

paragraphs.summary: 点明记者身处多媒体讲故事的新时代，而年轻一代视之为理所当然。
paragraphs.function: 总起/点题，提出全文核心话题。

paragraphs.summary: 春节假期作者抱着两岁孙子，带了一本简单的图画书准备读给他听。
paragraphs.function: 引入具体事例，交代故事背景。

paragraphs.summary: 作者拿书给孙子看图，孙子伸手用手指戳书页。
paragraphs.function: 叙事推进，呈现第一个反常细节。

paragraphs.summary: 作者起初以为孙子只是喜欢图画，孙子戳得更用力，作者困惑这孩子是否有问题。
paragraphs.function: 设置悬念，强化冲突。

paragraphs.summary: 作者恍然大悟：孙子习惯了一戳就会动的平板电脑图画，以为纸质书也是如此。
paragraphs.function: 揭示原因，解开悬念。

paragraphs.summary: 作者自嘲纸质书过时，但强调自己并未与数字时代脱节：会剪视频、做音频、用移动支付、还建过网站。
paragraphs.function: 转入作者对自身数字能力的自我评价。

paragraphs.summary: 作者坦言自己唯一的短板是很少出镜，但《中国日报》仍邀请他为京津冀一体化视频项目分享个人故事。
paragraphs.function: 补充作者经历，引出转折。

paragraphs.summary: 作者成了「网络明星」，自嘲不会得意忘形，但一定要让孙子在平板上看到。
paragraphs.function: 收束全文，首尾呼应。

group-2022-ii-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇说明文/新闻报道，围绕美国“开车发短信”这一现代驾驶陋习展开：尽管多数州已立法禁止且开展公益宣传，问题却愈演愈烈；为此立法者与公共卫生专家借鉴治理酒驾的旧思路，并提出用一种名为 Textalyzer 的新设备来检测司机事故前是否违规使用手机，以期改变人们的行为。

discourseStructure.summary: 先摆出已有的禁令与宣传（背景），再用“Yet”转折指出问题反而恶化（问题），接着引用官员观点说明分心驾驶持续上升（原因），随后提出“像治理酒驾一样治理分心驾驶”的对策，并具体介绍 Textalyzer 设备的工作原理，最后以推动立法者的话收束，强调用法律手段改变行为。

paragraphs.summary: 过去七年里多数州已禁止司机发短信，公益宣传也用多种方法劝人开车时放下手机。
paragraphs.function: 交代背景：已有的禁令与宣传努力。

paragraphs.summary: 然而问题似乎在恶化：美国人仍边开车边发短信、刷社交、拍照，曾连年下降的交通事故如今急剧上升。
paragraphs.function: 转折提出问题：禁令与宣传未见成效，事故反升。

paragraphs.summary: 部分原因是人们开车更多，但公路交通安全管理局负责人 Rosekind 称分心驾驶“不幸只增不减”。
paragraphs.function: 分析原因：分心驾驶持续上升。

paragraphs.summary: Rosekind 称“大改变需要大想法”，立法者与公共卫生专家因此借鉴旧办法，想把分心驾驶当作酒驾来治理。
paragraphs.function: 引出对策思路：像治理酒驾一样治理分心驾驶。

paragraphs.summary: 纽约立法者设想给警察配备 Textalyzer：事故现场警察可索取司机手机，用其检查操作系统近期活动，判断司机是否刚发过短信、邮件等违反免手持法的行为。
paragraphs.function: 具体说明对策：介绍 Textalyzer 的工作原理与作用。

paragraphs.summary: 推动 2001 年禁令的 Ortiz 称需要能改变行为的法律条款，若 Textalyzer 法案立法，人们会更不敢碰手机。
paragraphs.function: 收束并升华：用法律手段震慑、改变驾驶行为。

group-2022-ii-reading-d.overview: 本文是一篇科普说明文，介绍心脏专家 Dr. Ben Levine 关于运动改善衰老心脏的研究：随年龄增长心脏处理氧气效率下降，但中年阶段开始进行高强度有氧运动可以逆转心脏老化。

discourseStructure.summary: 文章先提出心脏随年龄衰老的现象，用橡皮筋作比喻解释心脏老化，接着介绍 Levine 的对照实验设计与结果，进一步说明开始运动的最佳时机，最后引用另一位专家对该研究的评价与建议。

paragraphs.summary: 随着年龄增长，即使健康，心脏处理氧气的效率也会下降，最早的迹象通常出现在五六十岁，不运动的人会更早。
paragraphs.function: 提出现象，引出心脏随年龄衰老的话题

paragraphs.summary: Levine 用橡皮筋作比喻说明心脏老化：橡皮筋久置会变干易断；但中年人现在开始锻炼仍可改善衰老的心脏。
paragraphs.function: 用比喻解释心脏老化机制，并引出运动有益的观点

paragraphs.summary: 介绍实验设计：选取45-64岁平时不太运动但健康的志愿者，随机分两组，第一组做无氧运动，第二组在教练指导下做高强度有氧运动；两年后第二组心脏健康显著改善。
paragraphs.function: 描述研究方法与对照设计及初步结果

paragraphs.summary: Levine 称把50岁的心脏调回到30-35岁的状态，原因是心脏充盈和泵血能力增强；而进行低强度运动者的心脏没有变化。
paragraphs.function: 进一步阐释研究结果及其生理原因

paragraphs.summary: Levine 指出开始运动的最佳时机是心脏仍有弹性的中年晚期；对70岁健康老人进行一年训练则毫无效果。
paragraphs.function: 强调开始运动的最佳时机，补充反面证据

paragraphs.summary: Dr. Nieca Goldberg 认为该研究是良好开端，但样本小，需要用更大规模人群重复研究以确定运动方案中哪些方面作用最大。
paragraphs.function: 引用他人评价，提出对研究的进一步建议

q-2022-ii-030.questionFocus: 考查代词/指代词义推断：末段画线词 something 在上下文中所指代的内容。
q-2022-ii-030.stemTranslationZh: 最后一段中画线词“something”指的是什么？

trap.explanation: 原文 something on the books 是“写进法律条文里的东西”，指法律，而非“建议”，原文未提及以建议来改变行为。
原文 something on the books 指法律条文，而非数据；Textalyzer 检测的活动信息并不是这里 something 的所指。

trap.sourceText: use the Textalyzer to check in the operating system for recent activity
trap.relationNote: Textalyzer 用于 check（检测）手机活动，易让人把 something 误判为“检测”；但 something on the books 指写入法律的条文，对应的是 law，而非检测行为。

trapEvidence.quote: use the Textalyzer to check in the operating system for recent activity

evidence.quote: We need something on the books that can change people’s behavior
If the Textalyzer bill becomes law

locationParaphrases.targetText: We need something on the books that can change people’s behavior
locationParaphrases.note: 习语 on the books 意为“写入法律、正式立法”，故 something on the books 指 laws（法律）。

locationParaphrases.targetText: If the Textalyzer bill becomes law
locationParaphrases.note: 下文 the Textalyzer bill becomes law（法案成为法律）进一步印证 something 指代的是 laws。

q-2022-ii-031.questionFocus: 考查标题归纳：需概括全文核心——边开车边发短信问题严重，应警惕用于检测的 Textalyzer 这一新对策。
q-2022-ii-031.stemTranslationZh: 本文合适的标题是什么？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 开车还是不开车？动身前先想清楚

trap.sourceQuote: So to try to change a distinctly modern behavior, lawmakers and public health experts are reaching back to an old approach: They want to treat distracted driving like drunk driving.
trap.optionText: To Drive or Not to Drive? Think Before You Start
trap.optionHighlight: To Drive or Not to Drive
trap.explanation: 全文讨论的是“开车时分心/发短信”及其治理，而非“要不要开车”这一更宽泛的话题，标题范围偏离主题。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 边发短信边开车？小心 Textalyzer

evidence.quote: An idea from lawmakers in New York is to give police officers a new device called the Textalyzer.
people are going to be more afraid to put their hands on the cell phone.

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 纽约禁止司机使用手持设备

trap.sourceQuote: who pushed for the state’s 2001 ban on hand-held devices by drivers
trap.sourceHighlight: ban on hand-held devices by drivers
trap.optionText: New York Banning Hand-Held Devices by Drivers
trap.explanation: 2001 年禁手持设备只是文中提及的旧背景之一，全文重点是新对策 Textalyzer；以此为题以偏概全，遗漏了文章核心。

trap.sourceQuote: An idea from lawmakers in New York is to give police officers a new device called the Textalyzer.
trap.sourceEntity: a new device called the Textalyzer (供警察使用的检测设备)
trap.optionText: The Next Generation Cell Phone: The Textalyzer
trap.optionEntity: The Next Generation Cell Phone (下一代手机)
trap.explanation: Textalyzer 是供警察检测手机活动的执法设备，并非“下一代手机”，标题把设备性质错配成手机。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Texting and Driving? Watch Out for the Textalyzer
locationParaphrases.targetText: An idea from lawmakers in New York is to give police officers a new device called the Textalyzer.
locationParaphrases.note: 标题 Watch Out for the Textalyzer 概括了原文核心对策——引入 a new device called the Textalyzer 来检测开车发短信行为。

locationParaphrases.targetText: people are going to be more afraid to put their hands on the cell phone.
locationParaphrases.note: 标题 Texting and Driving 对应全文主题，结尾 more afraid to put their hands on the cell phone 表明设备意在震慑开车用手机的行为。

q-2022-ii-032.questionFocus: 考查 Levine 提及橡皮筋这一比喻的意图，即比喻所要说明的对象。
q-2022-ii-032.stemTranslationZh: Levine 提到橡皮筋是想说明什么？

trap.explanation: 原文用橡皮筋比喻心脏老化，并未借此说明正确的锻炼方式，原文未提及。

trap.claim: The causes of a heart attack.
trap.explanation: 橡皮筋的比喻是为说明心脏随年龄变化，文中并未谈及心脏病发作的原因，原文未提及。
比喻意在说明心脏老化过程，而非保持健康有多难，原文未提及此意。

evidence.quote: put it in a drawer for 20 years and it will become dry and easily broken
That’s what happens to the heart.

locationParaphrases.sourceText: That’s what happens to the heart.
locationParaphrases.targetText: put it in a drawer for 20 years and it will become dry and easily broken
locationParaphrases.note: 橡皮筋 become dry and easily broken 的过程被作者用 That’s what happens to the heart 直接对应到心脏，说明的正是心脏的 aging process（老化过程）。

q-2022-ii-033.questionFocus: 考查两组志愿者在研究设计上的差异，即对照变量是什么。
q-2022-ii-033.stemTranslationZh: 就研究设计而言，两组在哪个方面不同？

trap.explanation: 原文描述两组的区别在于运动种类，从未提及饮食计划，原文未提及。
文中并未涉及志愿者的专业背景差异，原文未提及。

evidence.quote: The first group participated in a program of nonaerobic (无氧) exercise – balance training and weight training – three times a week. The second group did high-intensity aerobic exercise under the guidance of a trainer for four or more days a week.
evidence.anchor: 一组无氧运动、一组高强度有氧运动

trap.sourceQuote: Levine and his research team selected volunteers aged between 45 and 64 who did not exercise much but were otherwise healthy.
trap.sourceHighlight: did not exercise much but were otherwise healthy
trap.explanation: 原文说明所有志愿者都是平时不太运动但其余方面健康的人，即两组先前身体状况相同，并非两组的差异变量，选项错把共同前提当作区别。

locationParaphrases.targetText: The first group participated in a program of nonaerobic (无氧) exercise
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 Exercise type 是对原文 nonaerobic exercise 与 high-intensity aerobic exercise 这两种不同运动方式的概括，属同义替换。

q-2022-ii-034.questionFocus: 考查 Levine 研究的核心发现，即高强度有氧运动对中年心脏的作用。
q-2022-ii-034.stemTranslationZh: Levine 的研究发现了什么？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 中年人的心脏通过有氧运动变得更年轻。

evidence.quote: We took these 50-year-old hearts and turned the clock back to 30- or 35-year-old hearts
The second group did high-intensity aerobic exercise under the guidance of a trainer for four or more days a week. After two years, the second group saw remarkable improvements in heart health.
evidence.anchor: 做高强度有氧运动的第二组心脏健康显著改善

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 高强度运动更适合年轻人。

trap.sourceQuote: The sweet spot in life to start exercising, if you haven’t already, is in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility
trap.sourceHighlight: in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility
trap.optionText: High-intensity exercise is more suitable for the young.
trap.explanation: 原文强调开始运动的最佳时机是中年晚期，研究对象也是中年人；选项把适宜人群偷换为年轻人，与原文趋势相反。

trapEvidence.quote: The sweet spot in life to start exercising, if you haven’t already, is in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 人们开始锻炼永远不会太晚。

trap.sourceQuote: We put healthy 70-year-olds through a yearlong exercise training program, and nothing happened to them at all.
trap.sourceHighlight: nothing happened to them at all
trap.optionText: It is never too late for people to start taking exercise.
trap.explanation: 原文指出70岁老人训练一年毫无效果，说明开始运动是有时机限制的；选项称永远不会太晚，与原文结论相反。

trapEvidence.quote: We put healthy 70-year-olds through a yearlong exercise training program, and nothing happened to them at all.

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 我们运动越多，心脏就越强壮。

trap.sourceQuote: But the hearts of those who participated in less intense exercise didn’t change, he says.
trap.optionText: The more exercise we do, the stronger our hearts get.
trap.optionHighlight: The more exercise we do, the stronger our hearts get
trap.explanation: 起作用的是高强度有氧运动，低强度运动者心脏没有变化；选项笼统地说运动越多越强壮，过度概括了研究结论。

trapEvidence.quote: But the hearts of those who participated in less intense exercise didn’t change, he says.

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Middle-aged hearts get younger with aerobic exercise.
locationParaphrases.targetText: We took these 50-year-old hearts and turned the clock back to 30- or 35-year-old hearts
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 get younger 对应原文 turned the clock back to 30- or 35-year-old hearts（把时钟拨回），middle-aged 对应 50-year-old hearts，属同义替换。

q-2022-ii-035.questionFocus: 考查 Dr. Nieca Goldberg 对该研究提出的建议。
q-2022-ii-035.stemTranslationZh: Dr. Nieca Goldberg 提出了什么建议？

trap.sourceText: Levine’s findings are a great start
trap.relationNote: 选项借用原文 findings 一词制造干扰；Goldberg 说研究发现是良好开端，但她的建议是重复研究，而非利用现有发现。

trapEvidence.quote: Levine’s findings are a great start

trap.explanation: Goldberg 建议用更大规模人群重复研究，从未提及采访研究参与者，原文未提及。

evidence.quote: the study was small and needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people
evidence.anchor: 研究样本小、需用更大人群重复

trap.sourceQuote: needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people to determine exactly which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference
trap.sourceHighlight: which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference
trap.optionText: Clarifying the purpose of the study.
trap.optionHighlight: Clarifying the purpose of the study
trap.explanation: 原文是要弄清运动方案中哪些方面作用最大，属于进一步研究的内容；选项偷换为澄清研究目的，与原文意思不符。

trapEvidence.quote: to determine exactly which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference
trapEvidence.anchor: 弄清哪些方面作用最大

locationParaphrases.targetText: needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 Conducting further research 是对原文 needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people（需用更大规模人群重复研究）的概括同义替换。
